promptLatex: Two cards are drawn at random without replacement from a standard $52$-card deck. The first card drawn is a heart. What is the probability that the second card drawn is a heart?
hintLatex: Conditioning on a heart leaves a deck of $51$ cards with fewer hearts in it.
One heart has been removed, so $12$ hearts remain among $51$ cards.
solutionLatex:
The first card was a heart, so the remaining $51$ cards contain $12$ hearts.

The second draw is uniform over those $51$ cards, so $P(\text{second is a heart} \mid \text{first is a heart}) = \frac{12}{51}$.

Therefore the probability is $\frac{12}{51} = \frac{4}{17}$, which is smaller than the unconditional $\frac{1}{4}$ because a heart has been removed from the deck.
